body: **Summary:** Earn the spread: NII = loan yield minus cost of funds, plus fees, minus opex and credit cost. A bank is a liability franchise first, so cheap sticky CASA decides who survives a rate or liquidity cycle. Key metrics: NIM, CASA %, cost of funds, credit cost, GNPA/NNPA and slippage, PCR, RoA (the 1.7–2%+ franchises win), RoE, CD ratio, CET1. The cycle runs on credit growth versus deposit growth, the rate cycle (NIM compresses 1–2 quarters after repo cuts on EBLR books) and corporate/unsecured retail stress. Lead indicators: RBI sectoral deployment (monthly), RBI fortnightly credit and deposit data, SMA-1/2 trends, CIBIL/CRIF delinquency reports. Winners (HDFC Bank, Kotak through 2010–20; ICICI after its 2016–19 clean-up) grew deposits ahead of loans, priced risk conservatively and avoided concentrated corporate books. Losers (Yes Bank 2020, Lakshmi Vilas, IndusInd's 2025 derivative-accounting hit) grew loans faster than the franchise, ran a high CD ratio and had governance gaps. Valuation: P/B against sustainable RoE. Quality private banks traded at roughly 3–5x book in 2014–21 and now trade at about 2–2.5x. Nifty Bank was at 1.63x P/B and 12.1x P/E on 27 Oct 2026 (tapetide). Nov 2026: system credit growth is strong at ~18–19% YoY, but private-bank NIMs are compressing. HDFC Bank's NIM fell to 3.16% in Q2 FY27 from 3.26% in Q1, with credit cost at 0.44%, and PSBs are out-growing private banks on profit. Traps: buying RoE that leverage produced, ignoring the CD ratio, and treating an accounting restatement as a one-off. Sources: [1](https://rbi.org.in/SCRIPTs/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63891) · [2](https://ticker.finology.in/discover/market-update/hdfc-bank-q2-fy27-results-analysis) · [3](https://india.entrepreneur.com/finance/the-great-banking-flip-why-public-lenders-just-outsmarted-private-giants) · [4](https://tapetide.com/insight/market-valuation) · [5](https://www.indexpe.in/blog/nifty-sector-valuations-june-2026)

body: **Summary:** Capital goods and EPC companies earn by executing projects from an order book. Revenue is recognised on percentage completion, and margin depends on bidding discipline, commodity pass-through clauses and execution speed. Product makers (transformers, switchgear, motors) earn a better margin than pure EPC and need less working capital. Key metrics: order inflow growth, order book/revenue (cover of 2–4x), book-to-bill, EBITDA margin, net working capital days, operating cash flow conversion, mix of fixed-price against variable-price contracts, and client mix (government, private, international). Cycle drivers: government capex (central capex rose from ~₹6 to ~₹11 lakh cr over FY21–26), private capex (utilisation above ~75% triggers it), power T&D (the ₹9 trn plan to 2032), Middle East hydrocarbon capex, and interest rates. Lead indicators: CMIE CapEx new project announcements, RBI capacity utilisation (OBICUS), Union/state budget capex spend (CGA monthly), CEA transmission bid pipeline, Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding awards, PGCIL capex. Winners (L&T, ABB, Siemens in 2003–07; KEC and Kalpataru in 2021–26) bid selectively, kept their balance sheets light and moved toward products. Losers were the 2007-era infrastructure EPCs (Lanco, GVK, Punj Lloyd, Gammon) that bought orders with low bids and debt and then died on working capital. Valuation: P/E 40–80x for product companies at the 2007 and 2024 peaks; pure EPC 15–25x. The 2007 peak took ~14 years to regain. Nov 2026: L&T Q2 FY27 order inflow was a record ₹1.48 lakh cr and its order book ₹8.54 lakh cr (+15% vs Mar 2026), but operating margins are under pressure. Traps: order book over cash flow, and peak-capacity product margins. Sources: [1](https://www.investywise.com/larsen-toubro-q2-h1-fy27-earnings-presentation/) · [2](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/amp/business/companies/lt-q2-net-profit-rises-33-to-rs-5202-cr-order-inflows-rise-28-per-cent-1999332) · [3](https://www.downtoearth.org.in/amp/story/energy/power-demand-tracker-india-meets-all-time-high-power-demand-of-2708-gw-renewable-energy-share-34) Links: about `case_study:capital-goods-2007`, about `insight:transformer-peak-2026`

`strategy:ackman-quality-activism` | confidence: **verified** | tags: global, process, quality, concentration

Pershing Square's published criteria: simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses; formidable barriers to entry; limited exposure to extrinsic factors; strong balance sheet; minimal capital-markets dependence; high-quality management/governance; attractive valuation vs intrinsic value. Typically 8-12 positions. Add-on: cheap, convex hedges (credit default swaps in Feb 2020, rate-related options in 2022) where the payoff can be 50-100x premium. Lessons from failures: Valeant violated 'simple and predictable' (growth was acquisitions plus drug price hikes; reported 'adjusted' EPS masked it) - ~$4bn loss; Herbalife short and JC Penney turnaround failed on timing and execution. For an individual: concentrated quality buys on temporary bad news, plus a small, explicit tail-hedge budget (e.g., deep-OTM index puts) only if you understand options; avoid serial acquirers whose organic growth is unclear.

Links: person:bill-ackman (about); strategy:buffett-munger (similar_to)

Sources: <https://www.cnbc.com/2017/03/20/hedge-fund-titans-surefire-bet-turns-into-a-4-billion-loss.html> ; <https://moneyweek.com/economy/people/601185/bill-ackman-the-billionaire-who-bet-big-on-viral-doom>

- Credit ratings: ICRA and CRISIL fetchable; India Ratings / CARE not (use exchange filings).
- Alt data reachable: FADA, SIAM, npp.gov.in, CEA, PPAC, tradestat, Play Store buckets, Trends RSS.
